# Code of conduct

Keep UQ minis welcoming, practical and respectful of the students whose time and data it handles
This applies to project issues, pull requests, reviews and other project-managed spaces, and when representing the project publicly

## Work together

- Critique code, decisions and behaviour with specific, useful feedback
- Make room for different experience levels, backgrounds, identities and access needs
- Ask before sharing someone else's private information or using their account or data
- Respect another person's boundaries and a maintainer's request to stop or move a discussion
- Accept corrections, credit contributions and help someone recover from an honest mistake

Disagreement is welcome when it stays focused on the work
Nobody needs to disclose a disability, identity, personal circumstances or private student records to justify an access need

## Unacceptable behaviour

Harassment, threats, discriminatory abuse, sexual harassment, personal attacks and deliberate intimidation are unacceptable
So are publishing private contact details or data, pressuring someone for credentials, repeated unwanted contact and retaliation against someone who raises a concern
Repeated disruption after a clear request to stop may also lead to moderation

## Report a concern

There is currently no dedicated private project conduct-reporting address
For a maintainer contact, open a minimal [issue](https://github.com/keys-i/uq.minis/issues/new) titled **Private conduct contact requested**, without names, incident details or other private information, and ask for a private channel
You don't need to discuss an incident publicly

You can also use GitHub's [report content and abuse tools](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/reporting-abuse-or-spam) and block unwanted contact
Those reports go to GitHub and are separate from project moderation
For vulnerabilities or leaked credentials, follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md)

## Moderation

Maintainers may ask for a correction, edit or remove content, restrict participation, or block an account according to the severity and pattern of behaviour
They should consider relevant context, avoid disclosing private reports and apply the same expectations to themselves
No policy can promise absolute confidentiality or a fixed resolution time
If a concern involves a maintainer and no independent project contact is available, GitHub's platform reporting tools remain an option
